newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia hopes for trade surplus in Oct - minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia hopes for trade surplus in Oct - minister.

text.p: Malaysia hopes for a trade surplus for the third straight month in October, Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar said on Wednesday.
"October (figures) will be coming soon. We hope it is possibly a surplus," he told reporters after opening a seminar on interest rate futures.
"Inshallah (by the grace of god)," he said when asked to confirm if it would be a surplus in October.
"No, how can I commit myself," he said, when pressed further.
On Saturday, Malaysia announced a trade surplus of 668.4 million ringgit for September against a surplus of 604.5 million in August and a deficit of 280 million in September, 1995.

Affifuddin said there could be some inflationary pressures arising towards the end of the year due to the release of nearly one billion ringgit into the market in the form of bonus payments to government employees.

"The government has already taken pre-emptive measures. Like the government has liberalised the importation of food, which has the biggest weightage on the CPI (Consumer Price Index)," the minister said.
However, he declined to say if there would any change to the government's tight monetary policy stance next year as inflation is brought under control and the current account deficit drops.
"One of our major aims in 1997 is to manage the current account deficit as well as maintain a low inflation rate," Affifuddin said.
"Theoretically you have to tighten by decreasing money supply and by decreasing the velocity of the money. But, I am not saying that the government will be doing it," he said.
